topic: What if you got a five-star wanted level in real life?

script.text: Saturday morning, there's a knock at the door. It isn't an officer in uniform. It's a woman in a grey coat, with a folder. Detective Reyes.
She sits down at the kitchen table. Mum makes her a coffee, looking confused. Ellie stares at her badge.

'Thirty-seven police calls in four days,' she says. 'A candy wrapper. Some grass. A library book. A skateboard. All of them for one fourteen-year-old. And every officer says the same thing. They don't know why they went. They just knew where to go.'
She looks at the space above your head. For slightly too long.

'You're thinking of running,' she says. 'Everyone does. Last year, one agency, the US Marshals, caught more than seventy-three thousand people who were running. Most of them thought they had hidden really well.'
'I don't know what's happening to you,' she says quietly. 'But I know how this ends if you run.'
Then the TV in the kitchen switches to the news. The city's dispatch computer has a problem. It keeps sending police cars to the same street, all by itself. Your street.

At four stars, it isn't one police force any more. America has almost eighteen thousand police agencies, and around seven hundred thousand officers. And on the news, a map, with a little red dot that won't stop flashing.
The dot is your house. Outside, that sound you've learned to hate. A helicopter.

science.claim: The US Marshals caught more than 73,000 fugitives in a year
science.source: US Department of Justice press release, 'U.S. Marshals Arrest More Than 73,000 Fugitives in Fiscal Year 2023'

science.claim: America has almost 18,000 police agencies and around 700,000 officers
science.working: 2018 census: about 18,000 state and local law enforcement agencies, roughly 700,000 full-time sworn officers
science.source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Census of State and Local Law Enforcement Agencies, 2018
